violated_contract: A rollout flag must be declared on every deployed service that executes the code path it gates, or enabling it produces two different behaviours for the same user action. process_conversation runs on four hosts: backend-listen finalizes a live GKE conversation, pusher hosts the same path after 2026-08-30, Cloud Run backend runs it inline for POST /v1/conversations/{id}/reprocess, and Cloud Run backend-sync is the Cloud Tasks conversation-finalization writer for pendant/phone. The CONVERSATION_NOTES_V2_ENABLED, CONVERSATION_CALENDAR_CONTEXT_READ_ENABLED, and CONVERSATION_OCR_CONTEXT_ENABLED flags must be literals on all four. Omitting a host makes os.getenv fall through to the False default there. Turning the rollout on then produces a v2 note on one path and a legacy note on another — a discrepancy that reads as model nondeterminism, not as missing configuration, because both paths return a well-formed summary.
canonical_prevention: Enumerate the services that host a gated code path and assert the flag resolves identically across all of them in the composed runtime manifest, in every environment, rather than asserting a value per service. runtime_env_capability_contracts requires the three flags as literals on every conversation.finalize.persisted host and rejects disagreement. test_conversation_notes_v2_beta_rollout pins the per-environment values, asserts that backend-listen, pusher, Cloud Run backend, and backend-sync can never disagree on any of the three flags, and checks the deployed Helm values file against the composed manifest, since Helm reads the values file rather than runtime_env.yaml. The deploy validator's Cloud Run state fixtures carry the flags on both backend and backend-sync, so a deploy that omits them on the Cloud Tasks writer fails validation instead of shipping.
